sections.html:
Northampton Township doesn't conduct an inspection or require a certificate for the resale of residential property. That makes a sale simpler on the municipal side than in towns with a resale permit, though a certificate of use and occupancy is still required to occupy a nonresidential space.

Permits still apply to projects, including replacements. An old shed or fence may never have been approved, so replacing it needs a permit and a fresh look at current rules. Sheds of 240 square feet or less generally go behind the house, seven feet from the property line and no taller than 12 feet. Fences go in side and rear yards at up to six feet, never in easements, and corner lots and pool fences have special requirements.

The administration building is at 55 Township Road in Richboro, and the main line is 215-357-6800.

Northampton Township is a second class township of about 26 square miles in Bucks County, roughly 12 miles northeast of Philadelphia, and the Neshaminy Creek forms its entire northeastern edge. Its communities include Churchville, Holland, Ivyland and Richboro. Farmland turned into subdivisions in the second half of the twentieth century. The population was 6,006 in 1960, 35,406 in 1990 and 39,915 in 2020, so much of the housing dates from those decades.

Prices run high and turnover is slow. A typical owned home is worth $599,100, owners occupy 93.8 percent of units and median household income is $158,583. Students attend the Council Rock School District.

Route 332 crosses the township along Jacksonville Road, Almshouse Road and Newtown Richboro Road, while Route 232 runs north and south along Second Street Pike and Route 532 follows Buck Road. Tyler State Park offers 1,711 acres of trails.

Groundwater contamination from the former Naval Air Warfare Center in Warminster has moved into Northampton Township. The Navy has identified affected private wells and committed to some remediation, but the township believes more is needed and urges owners with wells to test.

The Northampton Bucks County Municipal Authority supplies public water to thousands of residents and businesses, and a public water connection project covers 334 homes. If you are on a private well, expect questions from buyers and lenders. Practical steps include:

  • Test the well through a laboratory from the accredited list the township posts.
  • Ask the Municipal Authority at 215-357-8515 whether public water is available at the address.
  • Keep any Navy or authority correspondence about the property with the sale documents.

The 2026 township real estate rate is 35.250 mills, built from eight separate levies.

2026 Northampton Township millage breakdown
PurposeMills
General purpose10.000
Fire services9.250
Debt service7.100
Recreation services2.930

Road maintenance fund1.000

Real estate tax is billed by the elected tax collector, whose office is on Bustleton Pike in Richboro. No cash is taken, and each bill needs its own check. Earned income tax runs 1 percent and splits evenly between the township and Council Rock School District, and the local services tax is $52 a year for people who work in the township. County and school district taxes are billed on top.

Appeals go to the Bucks County Board of Assessment Appeals, which accepts them once a year in early August. Any reduction applies to the following tax year. Find the residential forms and rules online, expect a filing fee, and visit the office at 55 East Court Street in Doylestown if you prefer to file in person.

You can also apply for the Homestead/Farmstead Exclusion by March 1, which covers the tax year starting the next July 1. Board meetings fall on the first and third Tuesday of each month at 10 a.m.

A buyer who takes title has 30 days to send contact information to the board under Act 29.

Transfer tax on a Bucks County sale totals 2 percent. One percent goes to the state and one percent to the municipality and school district, all due when the deed is recorded. Who pays is left to the sales agreement, and buyers and sellers commonly split it. If the amount is ever questioned, the new owner is the one responsible.

Personal checks have been refused for this tax at the Recorder of Deeds since January 2026. You can pay with cash at the office, a cashier's check, a money order or a card. Transfers among spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, and siblings may be exempt. File a Statement of Value (REV-183) in duplicate when the deed omits the true value or claims an exemption.

Should the state later decide the property was worth more than stated, the Department of Revenue bills the extra tax and interest directly.

Public water and sewer questions go to the Northampton Bucks County Municipal Authority, and trash and recycling are handled by the township's contractor, J. P. Mascaro and Sons, at 800-432-1616. A street listing shows each pickup day, which is useful to hand a buyer.

Commuters have limited rail choices. The TMA Bucks Richboro-Warminster Rushbus runs peak-hour shuttles from Richboro to the SEPTA Warminster station. The average commute runs 30.5 minutes.

sections.h2: From listing or offer to the closing table
sections.html:
Start with the deed, a payoff figure from your lender and the township tax bill. On a private well, book the water test now, since buyers and lenders here will want results and a lab needs time. Pull out receipts for any shed, fence or addition that needed a permit, and confirm each one was approved.

Once a buyer is under contract, the transfer tax is due at recording, and the township bill is separate. Pay the township bill from your proceeds and keep the receipt. Under Act 29 the new owner then sends contact information to the county assessment board within 30 days.

With a cash buyer there is no lender appraisal or underwriting, the stage where timelines usually slip. The deed, the well question and the transfer tax all still apply, so your closing date rests mostly on a clear title.

sections.h2: When a cash sale is useful
sections.html:
Cash helps when a house needs repairs you can't pay for or when the calendar is tight. Typical cases:

  • An estate property with an older kitchen, roof or heating system.
  • A house with a private well that failed a test.
  • An owner relocating before a listing could reasonably sell.

Weigh the cash number against a listing's net after commissions, repairs and the 2 percent transfer tax.

faqs.q: Do I need a use and occupancy certificate to sell my Northampton house?
faqs.a: No. The township doesn't inspect or require a certificate for the resale of residential property. A certificate of use and occupancy applies to nonresidential space.

faqs.q: What is the Northampton Township real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The 2026 township millage is 35.250 mills, made up of general purpose, fire, emergency medical, recreation, debt service, library and two road levies. County and Council Rock School District taxes are billed on top of that.

faqs.q: When is the Bucks County assessment appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Annual appeals are due in early August each year, and any change takes effect the following tax year. Check the county site for the exact date.

faqs.q: How much is the realty transfer tax in Bucks County?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent, with 1 percent to the state and 1 percent to the municipality and school district. It is paid at recording, and the buyer and seller usually split it.

faqs.q: Should I test a private well before selling in Northampton Township?
faqs.a: Yes, because the township reports groundwater contamination from the former Naval Air Warfare Center in Warminster. Use a laboratory from the accredited list the township posts and ask the Municipal Authority about public water.
